implementation_note: Second feature of the Grocery Rounds slice. Per-feature acceptance contract written before implementation per CT-7. implementation_note: Fourth feature of the Grocery Rounds slice. Joining is eight conditions holding at once, each naming itself on failure. The load-bearing reading: §4's ban on a creator redirecting pooled value is also about membership, so a creator may moderate and may never end a membership — removing a member holding credits redirects pooled value by another route (RMB-009). §10's guarantee that one member's default never reduces another's is made structural: recordLapse cannot reach validPurchasesMinor. NOT included: entitlement arithmetic, invitations as artefacts, identity, eligibility assessment, AML/KYC (review H5, still required by ACT-REG-001), notifications. No independent specialist review.

implementation_note: Sixth feature of the Grocery Rounds slice. DOMAIN_TESTED: packages/round-purchase-schedule implements generateSchedule/deriveStatus/recordAttempt/classifyForLedger exactly against all 16 acceptance criteria (tests/round-purchase-schedule.test.ts, 31 tests, npm run test and npm run typecheck green). Fills the gap left by GROC-F024: round-ledger already declares purchase_due/purchase_processing/purchase_failed/partial_purchase/late_purchase as event kinds and posts zero movements for the timeline ones, but nothing decided when an instalment is due or classified a recorded payment against it. This feature is the pure schedule-generation and classification layer that sits in front of it and reuses round-ledger's own LedgerEventKind type rather than redeclaring it. Late-join instalment policy remains an open product question — generateSchedule refuses rather than guesses (R3), per contract. LATE has no grace window pending unbuilt §15 reminders. Not yet wired: round-ledger's recordPayment still posts every payment as purchase_paid unconditionally — wiring it to this feature's classifyForLedger is P1 fast-follow work per the contract, not part of this gate. ACT-REG-002/ACT-REG-003 (payment capture) remain open; this feature is exercised against recorded attempts supplied by tests until they exist. The canonical Feature Security Profile classifies GROC-F023 as S2; no independent specialist review is included in this DOMAIN_TESTED claim. Defence-in-depth regressions cover late-payment classification, attempt idempotency, amount validation, impossible calendar dates, month-end dates and internally derived ledger classification. Deferred, not blocking: (1) classifyForLedger's return shape (kind + amountMinor only) cannot carry the per-pool split or vatMinor that round-ledger's recordPayment needs, so the P1 wiring from this feature into recordPayment requires widening the interface first, not just calling it; (2) no reversal/chargeback path exists once an instalment reaches PAID — a provider-reported chargeback on a settled instalment cannot be represented; (3) whether a FAILED status should be reachable after the due date (currently masked by LATE taking precedence) is contract-ambiguous and undecided, not just untested. Composes with round-plan/round-membership/round-ledger, all DOMAIN_TESTED.

implementation_note: Fifth feature of the Grocery Rounds slice, and the one DEC-003/DEC-004 land in. A projection over §9's fourteen events, not a second ledger — §9 requires reuse of the canonical kernel and CLAUDE.md forbids a second money authority, so this computes postings and owns none of them. purchase_paid moves nothing into revenue; goods_delivered is the only event that earns. Payments split per pool with VAT extracted from the price rather than added to it. RCM-010's invariant is checked from two independent derivations. Surfaced a finding: §9.2 lists a `refund` event that DEC-005 forbids, so it is refused with a remedy pointing at in-kind settlement — the same contradiction as the lifecycle's REFUNDING state. NOT included: the canonical ledger interface (unbuilt), payments, entitlement, allocation, the VAT return, persistence, and residual treatment (review H3 has no owner yet). No independent specialist review — this is the clearest money-reviewer trigger in the slice.
